content: Terconazole is a medication specifically designed to treat fungal and yeast infections of the vagina. It may also be prescribed for other purposes, so consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Terconazole is available in two forms: a vaginal cream and vaginal suppositories. It is typically used once daily at bedtime for either 3 or 7 consecutive days, depending on your doctor’s instructions. Follow the directions on your prescription label carefully, and if you have any questions, ask your doctor or pharmacist for clarification. Use the medication exactly as prescribed, without altering the dose or frequency. To use the vaginal cream, fill the applicator provided with the cream to the indicated level. For the suppository, unwrap it, moisten it with lukewarm water, and place it on the applicator as instructed. Lie on your back with your knees bent and spread apart. Insert the applicator high into your vagina (unless you are pregnant), and press the plunger to release the medication. If you are pregnant, insert the applicator gently. If you encounter resistance, stop and contact your doctor. After applying the medication, remove the applicator, disassemble it, and clean it thoroughly with soap and warm water. Wash your hands immediately to prevent spreading the infection. Apply the medication just before bedtime, as it works best when you remain lying down afterward. You may use a sanitary napkin to protect your clothing from stains, but do not use a tampon, as it will absorb the medication. Avoid douching unless specifically instructed by your doctor. Continue using the medication for the full prescribed duration, even if your symptoms improve. Do not stop treatment without consulting your doctor, and continue using the medication during your menstrual period if necessary. Before starting terconazole, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to terconazole or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription drugs you are taking, including antibiotics and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have a history of immune system problems, HIV, AIDS, or diabetes. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while using terconazole, contact your doctor immediately, as this medication may harm the fetus. If you miss a dose, insert it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not insert a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Terconazole may cause side effects. Mild side effects include headaches and missed menstrual periods. If these symptoms persist or worsen, inform your doctor. Severe side effects requiring immediate medical attention include burning or irritation in the vagina when the medication is applied, stomach pain, fever, or foul-smelling vaginal discharge. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. Terconazole is for external use only. Avoid contact with your eyes or mouth, and do not swallow the cream or suppositories. Refrain from sexual intercourse while using this medication. Note that an ingredient in the cream may weaken latex products such as condoms or diaphragms, so avoid using these products within 72 hours of applying the medication. Wear clean cotton underwear or underwear with cotton crotches, and avoid synthetic fabrics like nylon or rayon. Do not share this medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription. If your symptoms persist after completing the treatment, contact your doctor. Brand names for terconazole include Terazol® 3 and Terazol® 7.
